- Offer a 30-day dedicated burst (2x your current reserved pool) to run an apples-to-apples trial.
- $25k one-time credit to offset benchmarking costs and make the comparison neutral.
- Priority bench support from our SE team to run the tests and tune cache/priming.

Best,

Team — forwarding Pacifica's note. Quick ask: I need a tight bench plan and a recommendation on commercial concessions we should offer to keep the deal contiguous. Proposed offer (subject to your input):

- Technical: 30-day dedicated burst (2x capacity) + SE-led side-by-side using their production traces.
- Commercial: $25k one-time credit, renewal discount 15% for 12 months (10% for 24 months). No ELA required — standard renewal with committed throughput.
- Operational: Priority support and a pre-warm window for KV cache so warmup isn't counted against target metrics.

Ben — can you outline the test matrix (routes, sequences, warmup strategy) and an expected delta if we enable quantized weights + prefix caching? Can you run the bench within 48-72 hours of access?
Naomi — can you confirm their renewal timeline and whether we need legal sign-off for the credit?
Marissa — need quick approval on the numbers above (15% + $25k credit + temporary reserved capacity). If you prefer, we can tighten to 3 months of discount instead of 12 and push for a dedicated capacity requirement.

Quoting Aisha below for context.

---Original Message---
[Aisha's message attached]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 02 Aug 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal window — performance concerns and AltAI trial

Michael / team —

I can own the bench. Quick plan:

1) Data & Access: ask Pacifica for a 48-hour anonymized trace + example payloads. We'll run the side-by-side on identical hardware profile and model version.
2) Matrix: top 10 routes by qps, sample sequences at 95th/99th percentiles, two sequence-length cohorts (short <128 tokens, long 128-1024).
3) Warmup strategy: staged prefix caching with a 1-hour priming window to seed KV cache; measure cold vs warmed p95.
4) Optimizations to test: int8 quantization path, continuous batching thresholds, and prefetch warmup script. From prior customers I expect 20-30% reduction in p95 for read-heavy routes with caching+quant; on long sequences improvements are more modest but still material.
5) Timeframe: with access I can run bench + produce a report within 72 hours.

Risks:
- If Pacifica's peak includes many unpredictable long tails (very long sequences), the KV cache benefits will be reduced until we tune their traffic patterns.
- Any change to model variant during the test invalidates direct comparison. We should lock the model versions.

I'll attach the bench playbook and test scripts (bench-playbook.md) and a brief ops runbook we can hand to Pacifica.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[attachment: bench-playbook.md]
